full_judgment:
2. The opposite parties Nos. 1-3 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 253 of 1974 in the 2nd Court of Munsif, Kushtia, for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in respect of the suit land. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, was: The suit holding belonged to Rai Kishori Dashi who got it as a ayautaka stridhan property. She died leaving her only son Krishnapada Sarma. He possessed it during his life time and his name was duly recorded in The Record of Rights. He died leaving without any children and widow. After his death the suit property devolved on the plaintiffs who are paternal uncle's sons of Krishnapada. They have paid rents and got their names mutated and they have been possessing the same residing therein for over 12 years. Defendant Monomohini Dasi was the sister of Krishnapada Sarma, daughter of  Rai Kishori and she was married during the life time of Rai Kishori. She had no title and possession in any portion of the suit holding and she used to live in India after her marriage. Defendants No. 1-3 were claiming the property by purchase from Monomohini Dasi and threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs which necessitated filing of the suit. 

 4. The learned Munsif on consideration of the evidence on record and facts and circumstances of the case held that the suit properly was 'Ayautaka Stridhan' of Rai Kishori and the plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the suit land and accordingly the suit was dismissed. On appeal by the plaintiffs the lower appellate Court was pleased to set aside the judgment and decree of the learned Munsif, declaring the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs and confirmed their possession in the suit land holding that the suit properly was the "Ayautaka Stridhan" of Rai Kishori Dasi. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the appellate Court the defendant has moved this application before this Court under Section 115 C.P.C. and obtained the instant Rule. 

 (2) Wherever additional evidence is allowed to be produced by an Appellate Court, the Court shall record the reason for its admission. 

 6. Now let us consider whether the petitioners are entitled to the reliefs claimed in the revision case. Mr. M.A. Aziz, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the learned Court of appeal below has committed an error of law apparent on the face of the record in not treating the property as 'Ayautaka Stridhan' property of Rai Kishori and thus decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiffs reversing the finding of the trial Court in this regard. The learned advocate in support of the judgment of the trial Court submits that the learned Court of appeal below committed an error of law in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial court without adverting to all the points raised and decided by the trial Court and thus there has been failure of justice. On the other hand Mr. H. N. Nandy appearing for the opposite parties supported the judgment of the appellate, Court and submits that the suit property being 'ayautaka property' of Rai Kishori it has been rightly held as such and the judgment of the appellate Court having decided the point according to the provision of the law relating to devolution of property under the Hindu Law of inheritance is not liable to be set aside at this revisional stage. 

 10. Mr. M.A. Aziz, the learned Advocate for. the petitioners contends that the property of Rai Kishori was her Ayautaka Stridhan , as she got it by way of gift from her father and the property devolved upon her daughter Monomohini after her death in 1961 and Krishna Pada was in possession on her behalf and as such the land was recorded in his name but the court of appeal below erroneously held that it was the ayautaka stridhan of Rai Kishori and as such not heritable by Monomohini and the defendants have acquired no title and interest herein. 

 13. From the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record it is found that the suit property was the 'Ayautaka Stridhan' property of Rai Krishna Pada and Krishna Pada having died leaving no descendant the plaintiffs being the paternal uncle's son have inherited the said property and the learned appellate Court below has rightly decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff setting aside the Judgment and decree of the trial Court.
